page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n1 server family. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 15.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It utilizes a dedicated CPU allocation with hyperthreading enabled, and the processor includes a 45 MB L3 cache alongside support for AVX, AES, and FMA instruction sets. This configuration does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of this instance in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests rank in the bottom 25%, reflecting its older hardware generation. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks fall into the bottom 25% category. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression benchmarks register in the bottom 10%, while static web serving throughput reaches 2.46 GB/sec, also placing it in the bottom 10%. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the instance achieves 133.0 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model.

From a resource density perspective, the n1-standard-4 offers a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio suitable for standard workloads that do not demand high-frequency processing or modern instruction sets like AVX-512. The primary tradeoff is its lower performance-per-resource profile compared to newer instance families, though it provides a stable, dedicated CPU allocation. This server is appropriate for basic general-purpose workloads, including low-traffic web serving, small-scale database operations, Redis caching, and lightweight background utility tasks.
